sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and screen width
sections.what: Brings in the list, layout, icon, gradient, navigation, theme, and button pieces. Reads the screen width so slides can fill the screen.
sections.why: Slides need the exact screen width to line up when the user swipes.
sections.watch_out: The width is read once when the file loads, so rotation or window changes may not update it.

sections.name: slides
sections.title: Slide content
sections.what: Defines the four slides with a title, description, icon, gradient colors, and background tint. The slides cover documents, medicine reminders, the AI assistant, and privacy controls.
sections.why: Keeps the text and styling in one list so the carousel can loop over it.
sections.watch_out: Slide text makes product claims, such as family alerts for missed doses and the ability to change consent in settings. These must match the real app.

sections.name: OnboardingScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Slide state and Skip and Continue actions
sections.what: Keeps track of which intro slide is showing. Continue moves to the next slide. On the last slide, or when Skip is pressed, the user is sent to the login screen. Each slide draws its icon, colored circle, title and subtitle.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Tracking the current slide is how the progress dots know which one to highlight.
sections.watch_out: The current slide number is changed both by the Continue button and by scrolling. Changing one without the other makes the dots and the visible slide disagree.

sections.name: OnboardingScreen (part 2)
sections.title: Swipeable slide list and progress dots
sections.what: Shows the slides in a horizontal list that moves one full screen at a time. It highlights the matching progress dot and shows a bottom button that reads Continue, or Get Started on the last slide.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The paging list gives the swipe behavior, and the label change signals the end of onboarding.
sections.watch_out: The current slide is worked out by dividing the scroll position by the screen width. If that width is wrong on some devices, the dots can point at the wrong slide.

sections.name: OnboardingScreen (part 3)
sections.title: Layout and look for onboarding
sections.what: Defines the spacing, colors, circle sizes and text styles for the intro slides, the Skip button in the top right, and the progress dots.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These visual settings are kept together so the slides look consistent.
sections.watch_out: The Skip button sits a fixed 60 pixels from the top, which may come close to the phone's status bar on some devices.

summary: The first-run introduction screen for mobile, a swipeable carousel of four slides explaining what the app does and its privacy promise.
purpose: Gives new users a short overview before they reach the sign-in screen, and explains the data and consent controls.
why: Likely reason: explain the app value and privacy before asking for an account. The file header says three steps, but four slides are defined, so the header is out of date.
how: Defines the slide content with title, description, icon, and colors. The screen shows the slides in a horizontal list with a button to move on.
inputs: The slide content defined in this file and the screen size.
outputs: The rendered onboarding carousel and navigation to the next screen.
risks: The slide text makes product claims, such as reminders with family alerts and AI summaries, that must match real features. The privacy slide says users can change consent in settings, so that setting must exist. The header says three steps but the code has four. Only the first 57 lines were reviewed.
debug: If the carousel looks wrong, check the slide list and screen width value. If a claim on a slide is out of date, update the slide text here. If the button does not move on, check the navigation code in the remaining parts of the file.
